📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the best barn coats for men are a close cousin of the chore jacket—similar in spirit, but built tougher. They’re heartier, heavier, better insulated, and usually more water-resistant. Where the chore jacket belonged to the factory floor, the barn coat was made for the fields: a layer you could shrug on to tackle chores outdoors.

But ever since the ’80s and ’90s, the barn coat has been finding a fresh audience of urbanites who understand its utility, even on mean city streets. Today, alongside the waxy Barbour zip-ups and dad-approved L.L. Bean riffs, a ton of capital-F fashion labels—The Row, Auralee, Prada—have been herding the barn coat back into the center of the style conversation.

Reading to buy your first barn coat? Make sure it’s cut with enough room to comfortably slip a sweater beneath it, and that its craftsmanship ensures it’ll remain a reliable rotation beater for years to come. The former, of course, might demand some trial and error on your end, but the latter is exactly where we come in. These are the absolute best barn coats for men on the market right now, from the genre-defining joints you already know to the sleeper-hit versions you probably don’t.

Sources indicate that deep, easily accessed pockets? A warm corduroy collar? A charming plaid lining? This jacket from J.Crew is, quite simply, the platonic ideal of a barn coat. It has all the details dialed in, built upon a sturdy, 100% cotton washed canvas body that will only soften and feel more like your own in time. Originally launched over 40 years ago, there’s a reason J.Crew is still able to sell it four decades later. And we didn’t even mention the hook on the back, so you can hang this up with ease as soon as you enter your bustling, warm, overcrowded local bar. It’s the little things.

Industry observers note that I should disclose up front that I’m a bit of an OrSlow obsessive. I own more from the brand than I’ll ever admit publicly or privately and doubt that I’ve ever been unaware of something it’s produced, but this is because no brand has more consistently lived-up to pre-purchase expectations in my illustrious shopping career, and the only things that see the light of day are things that are absolutely dialed. And this jacket is dialed, folks. Made in Japan from start to finish, it has the kind of cut that can handle a Joey Tribbiani-esque volume of layers, is made from a cotton canvas fabric that will look unreal in half a decade, and the type of construction that other brands show factories when they’re trying to describe what they’re looking for.

We couldn’t round out a piece on barn coats without a nod to L.L. Bean, one of the OGs of the style. A century ago, Bean debuted a rugged duck-hunting coat that slowly shifted into a catch-all field jacket—the ancestor of the one they’re still selling today. It’s made from hefty, water-resistant canvas, with a sewn-in lining, five roomy pockets, underarm gussets, and bi-swing shoulders so you can actually move in it. And like many things Bean, the sizing is inclusive, there’s even a “Tall” option for the vertically gifted among us.

In a recent development, the Real McCoy’s is known for painstakingly recreating vintage garments—the Abercrombie set that Hunter S. Thompson made famous is an all-timer—so you can bank on the fact that this barn jacket has all the proper credentials. If you are dubious, however, know that it’s made out of a damn-near-bulletproof cotton canvas fabric, is fully lined with twill to trap some heat when things get chilly, has a perfect hit of corduroy at the collar and comes equipped with one of the sickest pocket configurations you’ll ever see in the genre. It’s hard to call anything “perfect,” but I feel comfortable saying that this is an ideal barn jacket, and would be hard to beat against any rubric.

Industry observers note that what’s all this, then—a Barbour as a barn coat? The Beaufort isn’t cut from the same stiff American canvas, but the brief is identical: a country jacket for tramping through fields, feeding the chickens, or—let’s be honest—making it to the pub. King Charles even reinstated the brand’s Royal Warrant last year (he is the Menswear King, after all). Built long before DWR and Gore-Tex, its waxed cotton shrugs off rain, the oversize corduroy collar blocks the wind, and you can zip in liners or snap on a hood if you feel like accessorizing. Best detail? The little hand-warmer pockets perched above the main ones—perfect for thawing fingers after a day of grouse shooting or a lap of the Lower East Side. Just remember: it will need the occasional re-waxing, but that’s all part of the fun.

If you're getting hung up on the idea of a barn jacket that’s implicitly unqualified to do barn jacket work, this isn’t going to be the one for you. But you if think that the barn jacket can be both a highly-functional, historically-revered workwear staple AND that it’s a brilliant canvas on which the most tasteful among us can mess around a little, this one from the maniacs (complimentary) at Auralee is hypnotic. The outer is made from a cotton moleskin—which is like flannel’s heavyweight cousin, for those unfamiliar—that’s been unevenly garment-dyed to look like it’s endured thousands of miles on a tractor. Meanwhile, the pockets are flawless, the zipped placket comes outfitted with a buttoned storm flap, and the whole thing is garnished with a detachable shearling collar, just in case you thought they spared a single expense along the way.

Knickerbocker is known for tasteful pieces that can help you rebuild an entire wardrobe, and that includes this faithful homage to vintage fly-fishing wading jackets commonly worn in the jacket’s namesake upstate region. The Portuguese canvas and rounded collar stand out among other jackets on our list, and the gusseted shoulders allow for a wide range of movement on and off the river.

First off, don't fear the red colorway. It's just as easy to wear as any other fall-adjacent color and it stands out roughly twice as much, which is kind of the dream ratio for eye-catching jackets. Also, it's just a damn-good barn coat, with deep ol' hand pockets, a wind-stopping corduroy collar and endless layering potential.

It has been revealed that this is absolutely a barn jacket. All the hallmarks are there, from the corduroy collar (more on that later) to the generous pocket situation and layout. But it's also one of the most stunning corduroy jackets on the market due to one of the most breathtaking corduroys you will ever see. And if you ever were wondering, why don't they make the whole jacket out of the collar, they do.

Filson's classic Barn-adjacent coat is an undeniable giant in the space—significant ol' stow pockets, corduroy collar, canvas outer—but the insulated iteration is every bit as easy to wear and twice as warm, without adding much bulk at all.

Recent findings suggest that think of this TS joint as the ultimate "what if." Like, what if, instead of a classic canvas outer there was a super soft, ultra sturdy, almost flannel-like flocked denim? And instead of corduroy, TS threw in a leather collar? Because across the board, they decided to find out.

According to recent reports, much like the Auralee number up top, this isn't the kind of barn jacket that you'd be wearing to bale hay, but there's only a select few among us doing that anyways. You can, however, wear the living hell out of this all winter long, because not only does it layer beautifully, it has the requisite storage, showstopping potential and only gets better with age. Is it practical? That's not the point.

Levi’s takes a no-nonsense swing at the barn jacket—exactly what you’d expect from them. You get a sturdy shell, a quilted lining that brings just the right amount of warmth, and two generous front pockets. Sure, it skips the classic hand-warmer pockets, but at a price this good, you can afford to overlook a detail or two.

According to recent reports, this is one of the most affordable options on this list, but you're not leaving a ton on the table if this is your prefered route. The outer is a waxed organic cotton that will hold up well against all forms of precipitation, there's a full flannel lining and the collar even buttons into a stand, to really keep things insulated.

According to recent reports, style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Sources indicate that our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

To kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

It has been revealed that we lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally new to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

In a recent development, whatever your preferences, whatever your style, there's bound to be a superlative version on this list for you. (Read more about GQ's testing process here.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on Saturday, November 21, Miley Cyrus married Maxx Morando—poolside in Palm Springs, with the ceremony officiated by the Flaming Lips’ Wayne Coyne. Congratulations to the very happy rock stars!

33-year-old Cyrus and Morando, 28, tied the knot in front of an intimate crowd of family and friends, underneath a dramatic archway framed by white florals and candles. (Because when you can buy yourself flowers, why not buy out all of Hollywood’s florists for your nuptials?).

Sources indicate that the bride chose Saint Laurent by Anthony Vaccarello (does this make Cyrus Vaccarello’s last bridal moment for the house?), wearing a long-sleeved silk gown with matching silk slingback pumps. Her jewelry was Chopard: Cyrus chose 18k white gold set earrings with 4.27 carats of diamonds, along with a white gold set and diamond ring. As photographed by noted bridal photographer Jose Villa, Morando, too, wore Saint Laurent, pairing a single-breasted tuxedo jacket and trousers in grain de poudre with a crisp cotton poplin shirt, silk satin tie, SL 970 sunglasses, and grained leather Lewis sneakers. While her blonde hair was in a chicly loose and twisted up-do with height at the crown, Morando’s was his classic tousled and layered mullet.

Recent findings suggest that in other photos obtained by People, Cyrus can be seen smiling brightly and wiping away tears as Morando shared his vows. Onlookers were dressed in all-black black-tie looks.

Cyrus’s mother Tish Cyrus and her partner Dominic Purcell, father Billy Ray and his partner Elizabeth Hurley, and her sister Noah were all in attendance. It was reported that the couple held their rehearsal the previous day.

On Monday—also Cyrus’s 34th birthday—the couple shared a new batch of images, showcasing the entirety of the day from the getting-ready process to the post-ceremony festivities. Alongside shots of the couple sharing their vows surrounded by palm trees, Cyrus also shared a photo of her Saint Laurent slingbacks laid alongside a monogrammed “M&M 11.21.26” handkerchief, as well as a snap of herself wiping away happy tears at the altar. (Also in the mix were images of Cyrus being walked down the aisle by her mom, and dancing with her dad at the reception.).

According to recent reports, then, there were a series of photos documenting the after-party, for which Cyrus changed into a black sequined minidress paired with sheer black tights and heels. Those heels were swiftly discarded, however, for dancing on chairs—before the happy couple made a classic getaway in the backseat of a vintage Mercedes.

Cyrus and Morando have been together for five years and were engaged in 2025. The bride previously confirmed that they first met on a blind date. “Well, it was blind for me and not really for him,” she told British Vogue. “I thought, ‘The worst that can happen is I leave.’” The pair went red carpet official at Gucci’s “Love Parade” show in November 2021.

Morando proposed to the “Flowers” singer during a vacation in Japan to celebrate her 33rd birthday. “I am not easy to surprise,” she admitted on Good Morning America following the news of her engagement. “I love to control every situation. I had completely surrendered. I’m telling you, I was so, so, so surprised.”.

Her engagement ring is a cushion-cut stone on a thick, 14k yellow gold band by designer Jacquie Aiche, which the designer made bespoke for the couple: vintage-inspired, romantic, and elegant.

Recent findings suggest that morando is a drummer for the rock band Liily (who played at Cyrus’s 2022 Fresh Year’s Eve special on NBC), as well as a songwriter and producer. The two have collaborated on multiple projects, including Cyrus’s 2023 album Endless Summer Vacation and her 2025 visual album Something Beautiful. Last month, the couple sang a duet of Cyrus’s “Let’s Get Married” on the Hollywood Bowl stage.

“I’ve always worked with the people that I love. And Maxx just inspires me so much,” Cyrus told Harper’s Bazaar of their creative work together. She added, “He’s very similar to me. We just don’t take life too seriously.”.

Congratulations once again to Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando!

Another bill to release Epstein files headed to House floor

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that massie will force another vote on releasing files in the Jeffrey Epstein case.
  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., enters his final weeks in Congress, he is one step closer to another vote on legislation related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
  • A discharge petition led by Massie aimed at extracting more files from the Justice Department has now received enough support to force a vote on the House floor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that massie will force another vote on releasing files in the Jeffrey Epstein case. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

As Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., enters his final weeks in Congress, he is one step closer to another vote on legislation related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

A discharge petition led by Massie aimed at extracting more files from the Justice Department has now received enough support to force a vote on the House floor.

Rep. John Garamendi, D-Calif., was the decisive 218th signature on the discharge petition, a procedural tool allowing rank-and-file House members to register their support for a piece of legislation and circumvent leadership to force a vote. Massie and other supporters of the effort say the bill is a bid for transparency.

Earlier this week, Massie stated his pitch to his colleagues was simple.

“They could be a hero if they sign it,” he said, as he chased down the final two signatures as the House returned from recess on Monday. Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., signed just before Garamendi.

Massie’s time left in office is ticking down after a challenger backed by President Donald Trump ousted him in his GOP primary earlier this year.

The petition marks the second push led by Massie to require the release of the Epstein files. Last fall, Massie and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., led a discharge petition on a bill dubbed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which directed the Justice Department to publicly release documents in its possession related to Epstein and his associate Ghislaine Maxwell.

Sources indicate that the bill passed the House by a vote of 427-1 last November, and in the Senate a few days later. Trump signed the measure shortly afterward.

In a statement this summer, Massie mentioned he believes the Justice Department is still withholding more than 3 million files that it is required to release under the November 2025 law and is “maintaining heavy redactions” on others.

The latest bill would allow state attorneys general, local prosecutors and victims to sue the federal government for withholding such documents. It would also allow victims to privately view unredacted versions of any records that mention them.

According to recent reports, now that the latest petition has reached 218 signatures, it must sit for seven legislative days before being called up by anyone who signed it. Last time around, Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., scheduled a House vote on the initial Epstein bill before that ripening period was over, saying it was a foregone conclusion that the legislation would reach the floor.

According to recent reports, other Republicans who have signed on to the petition this year include Reps. Nancy Mace, R-S.C.; Ralph Norman, R-S.C., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., none of whom will be returning next Congress. Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., backed the initial effort last fall, but her name did not appear on the petition this time.

In a recent development, allies of the glitch in Congress have faced pushback from Trump. While the president suggested during his 2024 reelection campaign that he was open to declassifying some Epstein documents, Trump then shifted gears, calling them a “hoax.”.

Sources indicate that “Once you get to 218, you can never sign it," Massie mentioned. "There's nobody left, no spots left. It goes straight to the floor, and then you can vote for it. But you were never part of the group that actually got it to the floor.".

Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken

💡 Key Takeaways

  • More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.
  • Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Recent findings suggest that whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a massive pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

Welcome to In Good Tech giant, where we ring in the festive season with fashion-insider entertaining tips, expert etiquette advice, and the perfect editor-approved hostess gifts.

Madame Isabelle d’Ornano’s early gatherings at her family’s Loire Valley estate were dressy affairs. Over time, the Sisley Paris matriarch—whose plant-based approach helped redefine the beauty industry—let the formality fall away. Grand dinners became generous buffets of moussaka, poached eggs over lentil salad, and even “pizza à la d’Ornano.” The mood is more relaxed now, but the thoughtfulness remains—a sensibility she shares in her newly introduced book, Imagine: Words & Cushions, and has passed on to her children, including Countess Christine d’Ornano.

Recent findings suggest that “I started to embroider the words ‘love’ and ‘peace.’ People wanted to buy my cushions. I noted no,” she remembers with a laugh. “My cushions are much, much too precious.”.

That sense of personal attachment runs through d’Ornano’s home, too. At 89, she lives on Paris’s Left Bank in a maximalist duplex layered with Henri Cartier-Bresson photos and objects by Jean-François Fourtou. (She shared the home with her late husband, Hubert d’Ornano, with whom she co-founded Sisley.) It’s also where she welcomes family for the holidays, a tradition that reflects her easy approach to entertaining: She likes a mélange of guests, from the glamorous to those for whom an invitation “feels like a treat.”.

Her family knows just how much the cushions mean to her—and still hopes to get one. “My daughter-in-law and my granddaughter say, ‘If you give me one present, give me a cushion,’” she notes. “Because I’m quite stingy with my cushions.”.

It has been revealed that if it’s a big party, the more glamorous people you have, the better. But you also need people who really like you, and some for whom it’s a treat to be there. It’s a mixture.

It has been revealed that I would not be able to live in a home that has been created and decorated by an architect, because I like having my mess and books around. You must not have too many rules.

According to recent reports, christmas is a wonderful tradition in our home. I made a cushion embroidered with “Noël”—it’s such a lovely word in French. Our family has come together every Christmas since I got married. And of course, we love presents, too.

In a recent development, bella Hadid may be the face of Saint Laurent and Prada, and she may own every high-profile runway she’s on, but her long-term life goal doesn’t involve spotlights or mega fame. In her new cover story for Harper’s Bazaar, the supermodel opens up like never before about what she sees for her future.

Sources indicate that “From an external space, success is about how known you are, how much you make, how many times you can be on TV, how many covers you’re on, how many fashion demonstrates you do. A cowgirl at heart, the Orebella founder has down-to-earth goals that do not necessarily involve modeling, but do involve having a small local business, leaning into hobbies that bring her peace, and becoming a wife and mother.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve always wanted to start a farm-to-table bakery, with flowers, and everything comes from the community. I want to do things that are fulfilling for me in my soul: having a greenhouse that I can garden in, having my glassblowing and ceramic studio, and having lots of children and being a mother,” she says. “It wasn’t a dream that I’ve always had, but it’s something that now is so intense for me. My intuition is screaming so loudly at me about it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bella Hadid has become one of the biggest supermodels in the world, and this year, she even opened the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show—a runway on which she has become a regular. However, her success is the result of a lot of work, and many rejections.

In a recent development, in her December 2026/January 2027 cover story for Harper’s Bazaar, Hadid opens up about a time, over a decade ago, when she was rejected after auditioning for the VS show. In a conversation with Bazaar’s editor in chief, Samira Nasr, Hadid is asked how it felt to come full circle. Nasr recalls: “On one of our first shoots together, you were really upset because you didn’t get the Victoria’s Secret show. And I remarked to you, ‘One day, they will be begging you to be in their show.’ And I could tell you didn’t believe me. Your whole body shut down. And three days ago, you opened Victoria’s Secret. Holy shit.”.

In a recent development, hadid admits that she often feels like she’s in a daydream. “I still don’t believe you, to be honest,” the Orebella founder says to Nasr. “I feel like people are just AI-ing me onto the runway. I think that it’s so crazy how time passes and you still have some kind of impostor syndrome.”.

Sources indicate that she goes on to add: “No matter how hard you work, there’s always another girl who is more deserving, more beautiful, and has worked so hard to be able to get that spot. Ten years ago, I remember that moment too, where I never thought I would get the show, but I think that God always has a proposal, and I truly believe at that time I wasn’t ready. I don’t think I’ve been ready until this year, to be honest. In past years, I was going to my horse-show finals in the morning, flying straight to the Victoria’s Secret show that day, doing rehearsal right before, and then pulling what we call a Bella, and Belinda comes out, and we just act. But this year, I felt really strong.”.

According to recent reports, over the years, Hadid has opened up about turning to an alter ego, named Belinda, to handle the pressures of her career. However, when Nasr asks if she feels like it was her or Belinda walking the Victoria’s Secret runway this time, Hadid responds: “You know what? Fortunately and unfortunately, I think it was Bella this year.”.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., leaves the Senate Republicans’ lunch in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., revealed Wednesday he plans to serve as the top Republican on the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee when Democrats take control of Congress next year.

The move clears the way for Senate Ethics Chairman James Lankford, R-Okla., to use his seniority to ascend to ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul at the moment chairs, and touches off several other shifts at the top of other committees.

The move fit in with Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s bid to use her seniority to succeed Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, as top Republican on the Appropriations panel. If Paul did not go to the top spot on HELP, Murkowski, R-Alaska, would be next in line for that committee in the next Congress.

It has been revealed that murkowski is second in seniority on Appropriations to Collins, who was defeated for reelection. But she faces a potential challenge from Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., who is next in line behind her.

Paul mentioned in a press release that he plans to bring the same approach to the HELP Committee as he did as chairman of Homeland, where he said he “challenged entrenched bureaucracies, forced federal officials to answer for their actions, and pulled back the curtain on what Washington tried to keep hidden.”.

He cited calling Dr. Anthony Fauci before the committee to probe the former federal health official’s role in pandemic-related shutdowns and the origin of the COVID-19 virus, and releasing thousands of pages of pandemic-related documents. The panel voted in August to hold Fauci in criminal contempt of Congress for declining to answer questions about the pandemic during a highly charged hearing.

Related: Fauci could face criminal contempt charge following panel vote.

Paul, an ophthalmologist, noted at HELP he will “stand against efforts to put Washington between Americans and their doctors, their children’s schools, and their paychecks.” He predicted “a rush toward socialism unlike anything we have seen” when the Democrat-controlled Congress convenes in January.

It has been revealed that lankford, in a separate statement, confirmed his interest in becoming the ranking member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. In many areas, he said, the panel can work in a bipartisan manner, and over the past decade he “worked across the aisle to improve emergency communications in federal buildings, strengthen the United States Postal Service, increase federal cybersecurity preparedness, government transparency, and the use of artificial intelligence.”.

Sources indicate that but he added that his job also would be to “push back on a [Democratic] majority that goes too far . . . Oversight is responsible, but obstruction is unacceptable.”.

Sources indicate that lankford noted he would work together with the likely committee chair, Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., “when we can agree and be a fierce opposition if there is an attempt to undercut our nation’s security.”.

The angular perspectives and planar aspects of the work that Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque created were adapted by Stine in her garment construction and softened her watercolor prints. Small touches deliver impactful results here. The addition of substantial beads on a drawstring miniskirt was quite charming and customized face buttons were cheering. The way the overbeading degrades on a blue check dress was nicely done, and the weighting of the top of the dress emphasized the swishiness of the long skirt.

Tech Report: Can 4 Minutes of Exercise a Day Really Improve Your Fitness?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (563 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, committing to any level of exercise isn’t easy, even whether you’re a gym regular.
  • Sources indicate that time may not matter as much as you think.
  • “The best four-minute workout is one that challenges your body appropriately.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, committing to any level of exercise isn’t easy, even whether you’re a gym regular. But a recent Penn State College of Medicine study may be music to the ears of anyone looking to get active with minimal effort—especially older adults. The findings suggest that four minutes a day of strength training helped improve leg strength and balance in adults 65 and older. The benefits are significant for study participants, but whether the results translate to younger folks is up for debate. Dr. Harry Pino, director of human performance and exercise physiology at Yunara, unpacks if four minutes of exercise can help make gains or if it’s all too good to be true.

Sources indicate that time may not matter as much as you think. But before diving into the details of your workout, Pino suggests figuring out your goals and assessing your current fitness level. If you’re unsure which exercises work best for your end results, Pino offers this breakdown:.

“The best four-minute workout is one that challenges your body appropriately. Intensity matters, but consistency and progressive improvement are what drive long-term results,” Pino tells ELLE.

It may seem insignificant and the warm-up may take longer than the exercises themselves, but Pino states four minutes can make a measurable difference, especially for someone who’s been sedentary. “Research shows that brief daily strength workouts can improve balance, leg strength, and mobility in older adults. These improvements directly support physical function and independence as we age.”.

The good news is yes, absolutely. According to Pino, exercise benefits are cumulative, and even brief sessions can stimulate positive adaptations when performed consistently. “Four minutes won’t replace a comprehensive fitness routine, but it’s an excellent starting point. Small, sustainable habits often produce the greatest long-term impact,” he says.

It has been revealed that focus on exercises that match your goals and fitness level. Pino’s recommendation is to start with a simple routine that might include 30 seconds each of squats, push-ups, step-ups, and resistance band rows, alternating with 30 seconds of recovery. “Prioritize proper form and gradually increase the challenge as your fitness improves,” he specifies.

According to recent reports, even a short workout benefits from a warm-up, particularly at higher intensities. Start with gentle movement to prepare your muscles and joints. Afterward, prioritize hydration, adequate nutrition, and quality sleep. Pino notes that exercise provides the stimulus, but recovery allows the body to adapt.

In a recent development, there is no one-size-fits-all workout routine, no matter your body type or how active you are. “Fitness level, strength, and mobility are much more important than body shape when designing a workout. Beginners may benefit from modified movements, while more experienced individuals can increase resistance or intensity. The goal is to challenge the body safely and progressively," indicates Pino.

The Penn State study only studied an older set of adults, primarily to understand how to prevent falls and balance concerns that can come with age. While Pino explained that these findings can have a positive impact for anyone looking to get active, he agrees that short workouts can be especially valuable for older adults. “They’re accessible and easier to maintain consistently. Even a few minutes of daily strength training can improve balance, mobility, and functional strength. These improvements are critical for preserving independence and quality of life as we age,” Pino indicates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

Industry observers note that if you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

According to recent reports, in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

Combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

According to recent reports, remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

Breaking: How Am I Supposed to Survive the Apocalypse Without My Phone?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones.
  • It has been revealed that many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations.
  • In a recent development, elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones. Last week’s tech outages––first, a failure of Microsoft’s systems, then, a national grounding of flights, followed by problems from Charles Schwab to Apple iCloud––were a reminder of how fragile our digital infrastructure is, especially at the dawn of AI. Preppers on Reddit, better known for discussing generators and the storage of food, began talking about how to AI–apocalypse proof the devices we’re all so dependent on. “getting serious about my preps with all the cyber attacks going on,” one user wrote. “I work for a security organization so I get a front row seat to a lot of the chaos. I’m specifically prepping for prolonged loss of power.”.

It has been revealed that many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations. “I had huge, huge spikes in traffic,” stated Jackson Studner, creator of Nomad and a student at Millersville University of Pennsylvania. (“I’m not a company or a startup, just a college student who enjoys building useful things and sharing them,” Studner’s website reads.) With the help of his professors, he built Nomad to provide some entertainment on camping trips and cross-country trips with friends. They’d hit a dead zone, and realize they wanted to watch a movie, or run video game software. Nomad is a miniscule server with TV and films, the entire Wikipedia library, and portable Wi-Fi, and offline maps. “I really like the reliability aspect,” Studner tells me. “I like to own my stuff. It's kind of that simple.” He’s also added navigation for his new community preparing for the apocalypse (or at least a grid shutdown). “It will actually tell you how to go along the road, it can tell you how to walk there, it'll calculate times, that kind of stuff,” he said.

In a recent development, elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber. Sherwood is best known for posting explainer videos showing viewers how to build their “homelabs”—personal, at-home computing devices—under the name Crosstalk Solutions.

In a recent development, the interest in Project Nomad, Sherwood remarked, has been overwhelming. “It’s got over 40,000 stars on GitHub, which means that 40,000 people not only saw the project and were on the page, but they clicked the little button to favorite it. And I'm getting over 200,000 views on the website per month,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that despite his newly introduced fans, Sherwood himself isn’t a prepper. He was inspired by the Information Technology Disaster Resource Center (ITDRC), a non-profit that goes into disasters and provides internet services when they are completely down. “I had the opportunity to go on deployment with [ITDRC] when Hurricane Ian came through, and I saw firsthand all these people that were offline. It was a disaster. Getting people back online was almost as important as the food and water supplies that were getting set up to help with the recovery,” he explained.

Studner wasn’t a prepper either–– at first. But since Nomad took off and he’s found himself in more “prepper” corners of the internet, his feelings have slightly changed. “It’s for peace of mind. I have my little go bag. I'm not too, too worried about it, but I like to know that if there ever was a real problem, I'd be okay in that situation.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that mississippi Democrat Scott Colom, here at a news conference in Jackson on Nov. 4, has defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. (Rogelio V. Solis/Getty Images).

Recent findings suggest that democrat Scott Colom has unseated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction.

The result is a stunning flip for Democrats in a deep-red state where they last won a Senate election in 1982, and it brings the Senate Democratic Caucus to at least 55 seats in the next Congress.

According to recent reports, colom was leading Hyde-Smith 49.2 percent to 48.7 percent — or by just over 4,600 votes out of more than 960,000 cast — when The Associated Press called the race Wednesday, a little over a week after Election Day. Ty Pinkins, the 2024 Democratic Senate nominee who ran as an independent this year, had 2 percent.

In recent days, as absentee and provisional ballots were counted, Colom had all but declared victory, repeatedly saying that Hyde-Smith had no path to victory.

According to recent reports, “I'll work every day in the U.S. Senate to build a future that generations of Mississippians can be just as proud to call home,” he posted Monday on social media.

Industry observers note that with his victory, Colom joins several other Democrats who flipped seats in deep-red states, including Texas’ James Talarico, Kansas’ Adam Hamilton and South Carolina’s Annie Andrews. Democrats have so far flipped eight Senate seats to win control of the chamber, overcoming a difficult Senate map and giving them their largest majority in the chamber since 2011.

That majority could expand further if Democrats flip the Senate seat in Alaska, where former Rep. Mary Peltola narrowly leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

Recent findings suggest that republicans have dominated Senate elections in Mississippi in recent decades. The last Democrat to be elected senator in the Magnolia State was John C. Stennis, who won his sixth full and final term in 1982. Colom will be the third Black man to serve as a Mississippi senator after Republicans Hiram Revels and Blanche Bruce during Reconstruction.

While Revels and Bruce, who left office in 1881, were elected by the state Legislature, Colom will be the first Black senator elected directly by voters.

In a recent development, colom has served as a district attorney for four counties in northeast Mississippi since 2016. President Joe Biden nominated him for a federal district judgeship in 2022, but Hyde-Smith effectively blocked his nomination by not returning a so-called blue slip, a Senate Judiciary Committee tradition that lets senators derail district judge nominees in their home states.

Sources indicate that senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer stated last week that he’d had Colom in his sights for several years as a potential Senate candidate, including for a race against the state’s senior senator, Republican Roger Wicker.

“I had Scott Colom and his father come to my house, and I served them a nice little brunch or something. I noted, ‘You got to run,’” the New York Democrat recalled to MS NOW. “They were smarter than me. This was four years ago. They said, ‘We don’t want to run this time, but we know that Hyde-[Smith], the incumbent, is so weak, we could beat her.’”.

Still, the Mississippi race didn’t capture as much national attention as other Senate contests until the closing weeks of the campaign. A trio of Black senators, Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland, Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware and Cory Booker of Fresh Jersey, all campaigned with Colom throughout the summer and fall. Key national figures, including former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, also stumped for him in October.

Colom’s campaign engaged voters with quirky ads and unconventional forms of outreach, including meeting with people lining up to attend a Trump rally. One ad that went viral played on Hyde Smith saying earlier this year that people had “so many proteins to choose from” when asked about rising beef prices.

It has been revealed that “Pick another protein?” states a man in the ad. “I’d rather pick another senator instead.”.

It has been revealed that major Democratic outside groups made a late play in the state, with WinSenate, which is affiliated with Senate Democrats’ top super PAC, investing $2.2 million. The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee spent $500,000 on a coordinated ad buy late last month.

Recent findings suggest that the pro-Republican Senate Leadership Fund dropped $1.7 million on the race, and Trump headlined a rally for Hyde-Smith on Oct. 26.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you can try XERF, swear by Therapeutic Plasma Exchange, or have your Golki bone-setting specialist on speed dial. But behind every Dorian Gray-style complexion—even those that have benefitted from all those cutting-edge treatments, and then some—is a humble skin-care staple containing SPF 30 or above. According to Carol Eisenstat, MD, founder and medical director of boutique medspa Line Eraser MD, “You can invest in all the lasers, injectables, and skincare you want, but if you’re skipping sunscreen every morning, you’re working against yourself.” The best sunscreens for mature skin, Dr. Eisenstat says, not only protect results of the very in-office procedures she performs daily; they also preserve existing collagen and elastin.

According to recent reports, “I think women can spend so much time looking for products to reverse signs of aging that they overlook the one product that can help prevent further damage,” she notes. Luckily, in 2026 the SPF market is rife with elegant, sophisticated formulas that transform daily application from a chore into, dare I say, a treat. (Personally, I can almost feel my skin heaving a deep, contented sigh when I apply La Mer’s silky formula on the mornings I’m feeling particularly luxe.).

According to recent reports, whether mineral, chemical, or some combination of both, modern sunscreen formulas represent a shift from purely “protective” formulas into multitasking products that serve as skincare, says Sandra Oska, MD, a board-certified dermatologist based in California. Made with thoughtful ingredients like hyaluronic acid, ceramides, squalane, and peptides, the SPF formulas dermatologists now recommend to their aging patients target dryness, dullness, and uneven tone, while providing the ever-notable broad-spectrum UV protection.

Industry observers note that with mature shoppers spoiled for choice, which formulas truly deserve a spot in your cart (not to mention, your beach bag)? Ahead, Vogue editors and dermatologists share the sunscreens they most recommend for aging skin. Sun safely!

What’s the best sunscreen for aging skin?

Because mature skin is more prone to dryness and sensitivity, Dr. Collins recommends seeking out a formula that not only provides broad-spectrum sun protection but nourishes the skin with hydrating and reparative ingredients. The sunscreens on this list, from dermatologist-approved brands such as Augustinus Bader, Alastin, and SkinCeuticals, check every box.

What to Look for in a Sunscreen for Mature Skin.

According to recent reports, “Skin can lose its ability to maintain moisture as we age, and mature skin often needs more hydrating skin-care products,” claims Jeanette M. Black, MD, a board-certified dermatologist and fellowship-trained cosmetic dermatologic surgeon. “This means that sunscreen itself should be more hydrating or be easily layered on top of a moisturizing cream.” (For instance, Roundlab Birch Juice Moisturizing UV Lock contains hyaluronic acid and the glycerin derivative glyceryl glucoside.) Dr. Black adds that any sunscreen should have an SPF 30 or higher and offer broad-spectrum protection.

Industry observers note that emme Diane Burg, an esthetician, skincare formulator, and the founder of Emme Diane Skincare, gives extra points to sunscreens that feature a PA+ to PA+++ on the label. “PA+++ is a grading system that focuses on UVA testing,” she indicates. “If you notice PA+ on your label, the product offers some protection against UVA rays, which are the ‘aging’ rays that cause damage and cancer. As the symbols increase, so does the level of UVA protection. So in this instance, the higher ratings, such as PA+++, are better in terms of sun protection,” she says.

It has been revealed that finally, a formula that’s fragrance-free, such as G.W.S. All-Over Sun Milk, is always a plus for mature skin. “In general, I recommend patients avoid sunscreens and other products with fragrances or other unnecessary ingredients that could potentially cause irritation,” Dr. Black claims. And for patients of any age who are more active and might be exercising or swimming, she always recommends a water-resistant sunscreen.

Are chemical or mineral sunscreens best for mature skin?

In a recent development, “Mineral sunscreens are the safest and the only type of sunscreen that I recommend for not only safety concerns, but also their ability to block both UVA and UVB rays for broad-spectrum protection,” claims Justine H. Park, MD, a board-certified dermatologist at Skin and Beauty Center in West Hills, California. Dr. Black adds: “Mature skin can mean that the skin is more sensitive, and for patients who might have potential sensitivities to the ingredients in chemical sunscreens, mineral sunscreen might be preferred.”.

However, Burg argues that chemical sunscreens can do more good than harm for mature skin. “Many people assume that mineral or physical sunscreens are inherently ‘non-toxic,’ while chemical sunscreens are ‘toxic’,” she indicates. “However, the reality is more nuanced. In certain situations—such as extended sun exposure or harsher outdoor conditions—a chemical sunscreen may offer more reliable protection. Physical sunscreens can be easily compromised if the protective barrier is inadvertently wiped away, for instance by sweat, friction from clothing, or even the straps of a backpack.” In short, she says, choosing between a chemical and mineral sunscreen should involve case-by-case analysis. For Burg herself, she oftentimes wears a mineral sunscreen on her face and a chemical sunscreen on her body, particularly if she’s spending time outside.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

Industry observers note that I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he said he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

In a recent development, take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

Mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Sources indicate that transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

It has been revealed that place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very quickly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

According to recent reports, do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

Is Friendsgiving the definitive holiday pregame? Actor and director Jordan Firstman certainly made the case in true Club Kid fashion with the help of Substack and A24.

Hosted in the actual Lower East Side apartment featured in the buzzy film, the evening gathered editors, writers, creatives, and Firstman’s inner circle for an intimate, home-cooked feast.

Pamela Anderson and Pandora amplified the lush, garden-like interiors of Palma restaurant in Manhattan’s West Village, transforming the beloved neighborhood Italian spot into a candlelit floral wonderland for a heartfelt Friendsgiving celebration.

Leading the resurrection of Urban Jürgensen, the revered watchmaker founded in 1773 that lay dormant until its revival in 2025, is CEO Alex Rosenfield, who played the role of consummate host. With this in mind, Rory Satran, the former Wall Street Journal editor turned founder of The Hamptons Chronicle, a “mischievous local print newspaper” distributed along Long Island’s South Fork, was a natural choice for co-host. “I laugh when people say, ‘What’s your distribution strategy?’ and it’s just me in my Volvo,” Satran told guests. “This past summer was great, and it couldn’t be done without incredible partners and friends, and Alex and his team are very much a part of that, as well as all of you here. I think the food is a star tonight, too, though, I mean, come on.” —Zachary Weiss.

President Donald Trump’s postelection statements about working with Democrats have presented the incoming majority with a kaleidoscope to decipher, but some Democratic lawmakers have their doubts.

On the one hand, the Republican president has contended that he can work with House and Senate Democrats after the upcoming Congress is seated in January, even floating a bipartisan immigration bill. But on the other, he promoted his hard-line aide Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff, raising doubts about any cooling of the political environment.

At every stop along his October campaign rally blitz before Republicans suffered massive losses on Nov. 3, Trump railed against “Dumbocrats” and their “bad” policies. He mocked their candidates as too extreme, too corrupt and too beholden to the most progressive wing of their party. He even warned that, if voters handed them control of the House and Senate, it would set off “a 1929-style economic depression.”.

In a recent development, voters ignored him. They handed House Democrats over 250 seats at least come January, and the party will have at least 54 seats in the Senate.

Trump was asked during a “60 Minutes” interview taped Friday afternoon at the White House if he could resist insulting Democratic lawmakers for six months if that’s how long it took to reach a deal on major legislation. “Very easily,” he responded.

But several Democrats are so sure about getting to a “Kumbaya” moment with Trump during his final two years.

Recent findings suggest that virginia Sen. Tim Kaine said it was hard to take the president at his word because he is “so unpredictable.”.

“But I'm certainly telling my colleagues we should try to put as many bills as we can on his desk that do good things for the American public, and then see how he behaves,” he said Tuesday.

Industry observers note that "We're gonna put bills in front of the president on affordability starting Day One,” California Rep. Robert Garcia, the likely incoming House Oversight and Government Reform chair, said Tuesday. “We'll have to see if he's serious, but I don't trust Donald Trump for a second.”.

The White House on Monday sent Garcia a letter, obtained by CQ Roll Call, warning House Democrats that their anticipated spate of probes "may cross the line into blatant criminality.".

Recent findings suggest that rep. Jim McGovern, a Massachusetts Democrat who is in line to chair the Rules Committee in the new Congress, said on the floor Tuesday that he does not see a GOP that is ready to heed the election's lessons and come to the bargaining table.

Industry observers note that “Instead of taking the hint or listening to the overwhelming majority of Americans who told them to change course, Republicans are doubling down on the same tactics and messaging they've been jamming down our throats these last two years, and it's a perfect example of why they lost in the first place,” he said. “They do not listen.

It has been revealed that “Then to double down even further, the failed lame-duck president appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of all the cruel policies that most people hate, as his upcoming White House chief of staff,” McGovern added, referring to the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. “What planet are these people living on?”.

Kaine said congressional Democrats might not notice that much of a change from the White House with Miller moving into the chief’s suite near the Oval Office.

In a recent development, “Stephen Miller was calling a lot of the shots, even if he wasn't chief of staff,” the Virginia Democrat mentioned. “So I view that as a kind of a change of the face, but not of the character of the administration.”.

House Republicans’ Tuesday vote to make hard-line conservative Jim Jordan of Ohio their next leader is another red flag for Democrats.

“White House Chief of staff Stephen Miller and House Minority Leader Jim Jordan,” Brendan Duke, a former senior Democratic Senate aide now with the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, wrote on X. “Where is the pivot to the center after a historic election loss?”.

Industry observers note that getting to the center is what retiring Nebraska Rep. Don Bacon indicates his fellow Republicans and Trump should be doing after the election massacre.

According to recent reports, "I do wish we could get to the point where we could solve substantial problems, instead of just beating the other side,” said Bacon, who has floated a 2028 presidential bid. “We can’t do this Republican-only or Democrat-only. And I would say this to the president, too: We’ve got to start working across the aisle to solve these problems.”.

Despite his postelection talk of working with Democrats, Trump has sought to blame them for an up-and-down U.S. stock market.

Industry observers note that “Right after the election it went down $3 trillion,” he mentioned Monday during an unplanned White House press briefing. “That was because of the result of the election, because the stock market does not want to see Democrats. And your 401(k)s have gone way down because of the ridiculous result.”.

Industry observers note that he's also returned this week to questioning the midterm results: “It's not even a result. It's almost hard to believe. Now, I wasn't on the ballot.”.

Recent findings suggest that members of House Republicans’ new leadership team on Tuesday sounded dug in and ready for a partisan brawl over Democrats’ promised investigations into the president, many of his top aides and Trump family members. Jordan's election as GOP leader shows that “we are ready to dig in for the fight,” outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters Tuesday.

Michigan Rep. Lisa McClain, who was reelected House GOP conference chair, pointed to Garcia's two-word statement on Election Day: "Lawyer up.".

It has been revealed that “Tell me how ‘lawyering up’ helps anybody with affordability?" she stated. “They're going to be focused on going after President Trump. We are going to be focused on improving the quality of life for every American.”.

To that end, retiring Maryland Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, a former No. 2 House Democrat, said Republicans should heed one big takeaway from the election: “Trump lost.”.

#169032. Toasted Orzo Chicken Soup

Toasted Orzo Chicken Soup

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (391 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chicken noodle soup just got way more interesting.
  • Any store-bought chicken broth, stock, or bouillon paste offers an extra boost of flavor to the base that chicken thighs and water alone can’t compete with—for an even more robust option, go for chicken bone broth.
  • More nourishing soup recipes this way: Curried Yellow Squash Soup; Broken Lasagna Noodle Soup With Spinach; Spicy Cod and Potato Chowder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chicken noodle soup just got way more interesting. Inspired by Egyptian bird tongue soup, this warming spice-tinged chicken broth is as comforting as it is flavorful. The real star here is the orzo. Toasted in butter until it’s deeply golden and nutty-fragrant, the pasta takes on a new personality. Unlike plain noodles, which quickly go limp in hot soup, well-toasted orzo stays al dente for longer, holding its shape and texture until you’ve doled out every bowl.

Any store-bought chicken broth, stock, or bouillon paste offers an extra boost of flavor to the base that chicken thighs and water alone can’t compete with—for an even more robust option, go for chicken bone broth.

More nourishing soup recipes this way: Curried Yellow Squash Soup; Broken Lasagna Noodle Soup With Spinach; Spicy Cod and Potato Chowder.

Season 1¼ lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs (4–5) all over with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Heat 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot over medium. Add 1 tsp. crushed fennel seeds, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. ground cardamom, and ¼ tsp. ground cloves and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 20 seconds. Add chicken, one 1" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or chicken stock, and 3 cups water. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Partially cover pot, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part of a thigh registers at least 165°, 15–18 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board and let cool slightly. Reduce heat to low and cover pot. Using 2 forks, shred chicken.

Melt 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup orzo and cook, stirring often, until golden brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Scrape orzo mixture into pot with broth. Increase heat to medium and simmer broth, uncovered, until orzo is just al dente, 8–10 minutes. Remove soup from heat and add shredded chicken, 5 oz. baby kale or spinach, and 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice. Stir until greens are just wilted. Taste and season with more salt if needed.

#169030. I Prepared for This A.I. Chaos Moment for Over a Year. Here Is What I’ve Learned.
